proposed_fix.description: Confirm whether packet loss/network degradation affects the ts-order-service pod or its node, and if confirmed, move the pod to a healthy node under human approval.
steps: Inspect the node hosting ts-order-service pods for interface TX/RX errors, drops, and saturation (read-only, e.g. ip -s link, node network metrics).
Check CPU saturation and conntrack usage on that node (read-only) to separate node-level causes from pod-level ones.
Compare latency of ts-order-service pods across nodes to see if the slowdown is node-specific.

If the node shows transmit errors or drops, cordon it (reversible) and, with approval, delete one ts-order-service pod at a time so it reschedules onto a healthy node; verify latency-50 recovers before continuing.
If conntrack is near its limit on the node, consider migrating other pods away (R3 'Migrate some pods to another nodes') before any limit change; treat any limit bump as a separate, approved change.
If no node-level fault is found, check network policy/sidecar or chaos-injection configuration targeting ts-order-service and escalate to the service owner.
preconditions: Confirm ts-order-service latency-50 is still elevated versus baseline (E1, E3).
Confirm the cluster has spare capacity on other nodes before cordoning or evicting pods.
Verify more than one replica of ts-order-service is running, or accept brief unavailability for a single replica.
Obtain on-call approval before cordon, pod deletion, or any node setting change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node (kubectl uncordon) and let the scheduler rebalance; if a conntrack or other node setting was changed, revert it to its prior recorded value.
